review_notes: I read the whole file, the `matrixOperator` definition and its simp lemma in MatrixAction.lean, and every use of `coordinateProjection` under OAI/NumberTheory/TwoPoint. `matrixOperator_apply` is `@[simp]`, but `coordinateProjection` is an ordinary def, so that lemma does not fire on it. No simp lemma describes the application `coordinateProjection keep v i`. I did not run Lean. Whether the `@[simp]` tag would help or hurt in every downstream `simp` call is therefore unchecked. I found no loop risk: the right-hand side `if keep i then v i else 0` contains no `coordinateProjection`. I report no other simp-interface issues. The other lemmas are structural (self-adjointness, idempotence, support, norm bound) and have no obvious canonical simp form.

findings.excerpt:
lemma coordinateProjection_apply (keep : V → Prop) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V) (i : V) :
    coordinateProjection keep v i = if keep i then v i else 0 := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical coordinate formula for `coordinateProjection`, and it is not tagged `@[simp]`. `coordinateProjection` is an irreducible-by-simp def wrapping `matrixOperator`, so the `@[simp]` lemma `matrixOperator_apply` does not rewrite it. Plain `simp` therefore cannot compute `coordinateProjection keep v i` and cannot reach the `if keep i then v i else 0` normal form. Every downstream use passes the lemma by hand, either as `simp [coordinateProjection_apply, ...]`, `simp only [coordinateProjection_apply, ...]` or `rw [coordinateProjection_apply]`. This is a recurring pattern across the files that use the projection.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. The left side is a head-symbol application `coordinateProjection keep v i`, and the right side contains no `coordinateProjection`, so there is no cycle. The desired normal form is `if keep i then v i else 0`. Then drop the explicit `coordinateProjection_apply` argument from the `simp [...]` calls in PrimeComplexMatrix.lean, ProjectedLiouvilleVector.lean and ProjectedGraphTesting.lean. For example, `simp [coordinateProjection_apply, paddingTestVector, hq]` would become `simp [paddingTestVector, hq]`. Keep the `rw` use as it is.
findings.benefit: Projected vector components then simplify to the `if keep i then … else 0` form automatically. Callers no longer need to remember to pass the lemma. The projection's behaviour on coordinates becomes part of the default simp set, like `matrixOperator_apply` already is.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] lemma matrixOperator_apply (A : ι → ι → ℂ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (i : ι) :
    matrixOperator A v i = ∑ j, A i j * v j := rfl
